summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update24.json → valid=true). Corrected the enumeration in the previous turn's shutdown-completion record rather than adding a new fact. The original said two request channels can hold an accepted request while the loop is not reading — the buffered apply channel and the verification channel. Re-reading the constructors and enqueue paths shows a third: the leadership-transfer channel is created with capacity one (api.go:570-574), and its enqueue helper selects between sending the future, the shutdown channel and a default that reports an enqueue timeout only when the buffer is already occupied (raft.go:2198-2205) — so exactly one transfer future can be accepted from the buffer without the loop receiving it, and if the loop then returns on shutdown that future is never resolved, the same completion gap already recorded for queued applies (with the buffering option on) and verifications. The correction also tightens the exclusion set: the configuration-change channel, though buffered, is filled only by the snapshot routine's future, which arms the shutdown escape, so it is not an instance of the gap. Recorded as a correction of the existing knowledge id with changed_premise explaining that the class is wider (transfers included) and the exclusions narrower, affected_uses empty because that revision records no uses, plus a successor interpretation for the same question. What changes in substance is small but real: a reader following the original enumeration would have concluded transfers were unaffected, and the transfer path is precisely where a stuck future also leaves the caller unable to learn whether leadership changed. The mechanism, harm (a caller waiting forever) and ceiling (client-side wait, no loss or reordering of stored data) are unchanged, and the previous counterevidence — shutdown documented as not graceful, at-most-one exposure for the transfer buffer, and the mitigation of awaiting the shutdown future first — is preserved.
